questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in the trailer, how should you clean it?
questions.explanation: Wash all parts exposed to corrosive materials thoroughly with water.

questions.question: Unbaffled tanks are also called ____ tanks.
questions.explanation: Unbaffled tanks are often called "smooth bore tanks."

questions.question: Where should you load and unload hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Heat can make many hazardous materials more dangerous. Always load and unload hazardous materials away from heat sources.

questions.question: In an emergency situation, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice in an emergency. Steering out of the way is usually safer than stopping to avoid a crash.

questions.question: Is texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle allowed?

options.text: Yes, if the text is work-related.
Yes, if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Yes, because it is safer than talking on the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing or reading text on any electronic device.

questions.question: How should you check your vehicle's lights before driving?

options.text: The engine should be running and the vehicle in gear.
Check the lights from inside the vehicle.
Check the lights using a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.explanation: Before checking lights, set the parking brake, turn off the engine, and remove the key. Turn on the low beam headlights and flashers. Get out of the vehicle and look at each light to make sure they work.

questions.question: When making a tight maneuver, how often should you use your mirrors?

options.text: Do not use them, as they are distracting.
Use them, but not too often.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade, your brakes may fade. What does this mean?

options.text: They work differently on the front and back wheels.

questions.explanation: Using brakes too much on a steep downgrade causes them to overheat and work poorly. Use engine braking instead to prevent brake fade on steep hills.

questions.question: When do you need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Only in a vehicle requiring a Class A license.
Only in a vehicle requiring a Class B license.
Only in a vehicle requiring a Class C license.

questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance are difficult to drive over:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be difficult to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Low-slung trailers and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially challenging to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand so you can eat or drink.
With one hand at a time, switching hands.
With a cracked grip for better control.

questions.explanation: Always hold the steering wheel with both hands. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel for better control.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and blocking other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Check local laws to make sure emergency flashers are allowed.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, you should:

options.text: Let go of the steering wheel.
Do not brake and let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake and let the vehicle slow down on its own.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down naturally. Once it has slowed down a lot, brake gently and pull off the road.

questions.question: What should you do if the third column of the Hazardous Materials Table says "Forbidden"?

options.text: Transport it with a security guard.

questions.explanation: The third column of the Hazardous Materials Table lists the hazard class. Never transport any material marked as "Forbidden."

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver involved in a crash ahead, you should:

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop safely and tell police about the driver's aggressive behavior.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely and tell police about the driver's aggressive behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away. Wait for police and tell them what you saw.

questions.question: When checking a tank vehicle, the most important thing is to verify:

options.text: There is no frost on the windshield.

questions.explanation: Tank vehicles need careful inspection. The most important thing to check is that there are no leaks. Check your vehicle's manual for a complete inspection list.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand brake during a trailer jackknife will:
questions.explanation: If your trailer is jackknifing, release the brakes to help your tires grip the road. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Swerving around a hazard is sometimes safer than stopping. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of drowsiness?
questions.explanation: Never drive when drowsy. Warning signs include blinking often, your eyes closing on their own, yawning, and drifting between lanes.
